hero.artist: The map is by Alvin Jewett Johnson (1827-1884), and was published in 1864. TwoScarsUp made modifications.
hero.credit: This is a crop from Johnson's Virginia, Delaware, Maryland & Virginia map published in 1864. It can be found in the U.S. Library of Congress here. Labels and arrows have been added by TwoScarsUp based on the book named "The Battle of Charleston and the 1862 Kanawha Valley Campaign" by Terry Lowry. A map on page 40 of the book is comparable to this map, and Chapter 2 "Jenkins' Trans-Allegheny Raid August-September 1862" on page 41 through 75 contains detail.
hero.description: This map shows the route of Confederate Brigadier General Albert G. Jenkins in the Kanawha Valley Campaign of 1862 during the American Civil War. Jenkins circled behind a Union force commanded by Colonel Joseph Andrew Jackson Lightburn while a larger Confederate force commanded by Major General William W. Loring occupied the front.
categories: Jenkins' Western Virginia and Ohio Raid of 1862

gallery.title: File:Western Virginia 1862.png
gallery.artist: Jacob Dolson Cox modified by TwoScarsUp
gallery.credit: This is a portion of a map from page 41 of the book "Military Reminiscences of the Civil War", by Jacob Dolson Cox. It was published in 1900. The map has been modified with a label and highlighting of the Kanawha River Valley and important points nearby..
gallery.description: Map shows western Virginia (eventually West Virginia) in 1862, with the Kanawha River Valley and nearby important points highlighted. In 1862 during the American Civil War, a group of small battles were fought in the region, including at Charleston.
categories: Details of old maps of West Virginia

gallery.title: File:LightburnEscapes2.png
gallery.artist: The map is by Alvin Jewett Johnson (1827-1884), and was published in 1864. TwoScarsUp made modifications.
gallery.credit: This is a crop from Johnson's Virginia, Delaware, Maryland & Virginia map published in 1864. It can be found in the U.S. Library of Congress here. Labels and highlighting have been added by TwoScarsUp based on the book named "The Battle of Charleston and the 1862 Kanawha Valley Campaign" by Terry Lowry. Chapter 8 (beginning on page 239) discusses the retreat from Charleston to the Ohio River. Pages 208 and 209 discuss Lightburn's decision to take the Ripley Road north instead of the direct route to Point Pleasant.
gallery.description: This map shows the route of Union Colonel Joseph A. J. Lightburn's retreat from Charleston in the Kanawha Valley Campaign of 1862 during the American Civil War. Lightburn took a route to Ripley and Ravenswood to get to Ohio, and then moved to Point Pleasant. This avoided possible Confederate troops at Coalsmouth, and the cannon fire from Confederate troops on the south side of the Kanawha River.
categories: Jenkins' Western Virginia and Ohio Raid of 1862
